```markdown
# User Data Export — Implementation Tasks

Source: PM-approved plan (2026-10-11). Target: ship week of 2026-10-19.

## Working Assumptions (confirm with PM — each one changes scope)
- [ ] **A1 Who can export:** Only the authenticated user can export their own data. No admin or support access in v1.
- [ ] **A2 "All data":** Means every user-owned record in our primary datastores (profile, settings, user-generated content, activity history). Excludes derived/internal data (fraud scores, internal notes) and third-party processor data.
- [ ] **A3 Format:** JSON. It is easiest and machine-readable, which covers GDPR Art. 20 portability. One file per entity type, zipped.
- [ ] **A4 "Fast":** The request returns immediately with a job ID. The export runs async and is ready within 1 hour for 99% of users. A synchronous response won't work for heavy users.
- [ ] **A5 Delivery:** The finished export goes to object storage and is served by a signed URL that expires in 24h. The user is notified by email or in-app.
- [ ] **A6 Rate limit:** 1 export per user per 24h.

## Phase 1 — Data Inventory (blocks everything else)
- [ ] T1. List every table/collection/service that holds user-owned data, with the user-ID join key for each. Owner: ___
- [ ] T2. Mark which fields are included, excluded (internal), or redacted (e.g. other users' PII inside shared threads, secrets, password hashes).
- [ ] T3. Get privacy/legal sign-off on the include/exclude list (fast review; A2 depends on it).

## Phase 2 — API & Job Infrastructure
- [ ] T4. `POST /v1/users/me/exports` creates an export job and returns `202 {job_id}`. Requires auth; the user can only target self (A1).
- [ ] T5. `GET /v1/users/me/exports/{job_id}` returns status (`pending|running|complete|failed`) and the signed URL once complete.
- [ ] T6. Export job table: id, user_id, status, timestamps, file location, error.
- [ ] T7. Per-user rate limit and dedupe so only one active job exists per user (A6).
- [ ] T8. Background worker that consumes export jobs from the queue.

## Phase 3 — Export Generation
- [ ] T9. One exporter per data source from T1. Stream/paginate the reads; never load everything into memory.
- [ ] T10. JSON serialization with a documented schema and a `manifest.json` (export version, generated_at, file list).
- [ ] T11. Zip the output and upload it to a private bucket with encryption at rest.
- [ ] T12. Generate the signed URL (24h TTL) and run a cleanup job that deletes expired exports (A5).
- [ ] T13. Notify the user when the export is ready.

## Phase 4 — Security & Compliance
- [ ] T14. Authorization tests: user A cannot create, read, or download user B's export (IDOR checks on every endpoint and the URL).
- [ ] T15. Audit log entry for each export request and each download.
- [ ] T16. Confirm no excluded or redacted fields leak, using a fixture user with data in every source.
- [ ] T17. Consider re-auth or a recent-login check before export (high-value target if an account is compromised).

## Phase 5 — Performance & Reliability
- [ ] T18. Load test with a largest-realistic-user fixture to validate A4 timing.
- [ ] T19. Retry with backoff on worker failure; mark the job `failed` after N attempts; alert on failure rate.
- [ ] T20. Metrics: job duration, size, and failure count.

## Phase 6 — Ship
- [ ] T21. API docs plus a user-facing help article describing the contents and format.
- [ ] T22. Feature flag; roll out to internal users first, then GA.
- [ ] T23. Runbook: stuck jobs, manual re-trigger, purge.

## Critical Path
T1 → T2 → T9 → T16 → T22. Phase 2 can proceed in parallel with T1 to T3.
Biggest schedule risk: T1/T3. If the data inventory is large, scope v1 to the core sources and track the rest as follow-ups.
```

---

**Why the assumptions are there:** "Export all of a user's data" touches PII and authorization, and if it's a GDPR/CCPA response it also has legal obligations. "Fast" and "whatever format" can't be tested as written. If the PM confirms A1 through A6 as-is, nothing above changes and you're unblocked. If any answer differs, tell me which one and I'll adjust the affected tasks.
